chunks: Ali, from his father, from Muhsin ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Hammad, from Yunus ibn Hammad, from Yunus ibn Yaqub, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When the deceased dies, they gather at his presence asking him about those who have passed away and those who remain. So if one had died and did not come to them, they say, 'He has perished, he has perished.' And some of them say to others, 'Leave him until he settles from what has passed upon him from death.'

key_terms.عَمَّنْ مَضَى: About those who have passed away

ai.seo_question: What happens to the soul of the deceased immediately after death according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the social continuity of the soul in the Barzakh, where newly deceased believers are greeted by their predecessors who seek news of the living and the dead. The detail about advising patience until the 'shock of death' subsides reflects the Shia understanding of the soul's transition period, emphasizing that the initial disorientation is temporary and that the community of the faithful remains interconnected beyond physical death. This underscores the concept of the 'World of Souls' (Alam al-Arwah) as a dynamic realm of communication and recognition.

en.hubeali:
Ali, from his father, from Muhsin Bin Ahmad, from Muhammad Bin Hammad, from Yunush Bin Yaqoub, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘When the deceased dies, they (souls of the Believers) gather in his presence asking him about the ones who passed away and the ones who remain. So if one had died and did not come to them, they are saying, ‘Perished! Perished! And some of them are saying to the others, ‘Leave it until it settles from what has passed upon it, from the (experience of) death’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali has narrated from his father from Muhsin ibn Ahmad from Muhammad ibn Hammad from Yunus ibn Ya‘qub who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that

when a dying person dies, other spirits gather around him and ask, ‘Who is still alive and who is dead?’ If someone is dead and has not joined them they say, ‘He then has fallen into the deep.’ Others among them say, ‘Leave him alone so he can gain comfort from what he has experienced from death.’”
